title: Components of a w-local space
statement:
Let $T$ be a spectral space whose set $T^c$ of closed points is closed.

1. $T^c$, with the subspace topology, is profinite.
2. If every point of $T$ specializes to exactly one closed point, then the map
   $r\colon T\to T^c$ sending a point to its closed specialization is a continuous
   retraction; the connected components of $T$ are the fibres
   $r^{-1}(c)=\{\text{generalizations of }c\}$, $c\in T^c$; and the composite
   $T^c\hookrightarrow T\to\pi_0(T)$ is a homeomorphism; in particular $\pi_0(T)$ is profinite.
3. Conversely, if every connected component of $T$ contains exactly one closed point, then
   every point of $T$ specializes to exactly one closed point. Hence the definition of
   w-local in [sk-def-pe-wlocal] agrees with [def-weil-pbc-w-local].
4. For $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ w-local and $\mathfrak m\in T^c$, the component of
   $\mathfrak m$ is the image of $\operatorname{Spec}R_{\mathfrak m}\to\operatorname{Spec}R$.

proof.text: Put $S=T^c$ with its subspace topology. Since $S$ is closed in the spectral space $T$, [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-closed-subspace] makes $S$ spectral. Each singleton of $S$ is closed, since it is the trace of a closed singleton of $T$. Thus $S$ has no nontrivial specializations.

source.place: Tag 0902, lemma-spectral-sub, closed-subspace case; Tag 0905, lemma-characterize-profinite-spectral, (6) implies (5)

proof.text: Let $U$ be a quasi-compact open subset of $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-open-retrocompact-iff-quasi-compact] it is retrocompact, hence constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset]: use the single term $U\cap(S\setminus\varnothing)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-proconstructible-closure-specialization] to the one-member family $E_*=U$. Every $x\in\overline U$ is a specialization of some $u\in U$; since $S$ has closed singletons, $x=u$. Thus $\overline U=U$, so every quasi-compact open of $S$ is clopen.

By the definition of spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space], $S$ is quasi-compact and its quasi-compact opens form a basis. Sobriety implies $T_0$: two topologically indistinguishable points would both be generic points of the same irreducible closed singleton closure. Hence distinct points of $S$ are separated by a basis open $U$ containing exactly one; $U$ and its complement are disjoint open neighbourhoods. This makes $S$ Hausdorff. Any connected subset containing two distinct points would be separated by the same clopen $U$ and its complement. Therefore $S$ is totally disconnected. Being quasi-compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected is precisely being profinite, proving clause 1.

source.place: Tag 0905, lemma-characterize-profinite-spectral, (4) implies (2) and the final paragraph; the separation arguments written out

proof.text: For every $x\in T$, apply [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point] to the nonempty closed subset $\overline{\{x\}}$ of $T$. Its hypotheses hold: $T$ is quasi-compact and sober, hence $T_0$ as in step 3. It supplies a point $c\in\overline{\{x\}}$ closed in $T$, so $x$ specializes to $c$. Also $\overline{\{x\}}$ is connected: in a separation into two relatively open nonempty parts, $x$ lies in one part, while every nonempty relatively open subset of its closure must contain $x$, contradicting disjointness. Consequently $x$ and every specialization of $x$ lie in the same connected component.

source.place: Tag 005E, lemma-quasi-compact-closed-point; used in proetale.tex Tag 0968, lemma-spectral-split; connectedness of a singleton closure written out

proof.text: Assume now that closed specializations are unique. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-w-local-closed-points-components-homeomorphism] hold: $T$ is spectral, $S$ is closed, and two closed specializations of one point are equal. Thus the canonical map $h:S\to\pi_0(T)$ is a homeomorphism. Write $q:T\to\pi_0(T)$ for the continuous quotient map and define $r=h^{-1}\circ q$. If $c$ is the closed specialization of $x$, step 4 gives $q(x)=q(c)=h(c)$, so $r(x)=c$. This both identifies $r$ with the asserted specialization map and proves its continuity. For $c\in S$, $q(c)=h(c)$ gives $r(c)=c$, so it is a retraction. Since $h$ is bijective, $r^{-1}(c)=q^{-1}(h(c))$, exactly the connected component of $c$; by the preceding identification this is exactly the generalizations of $c$. Finally $h$ transports the compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topology established in clause 1 to $\pi_0(T)$. This proves every assertion of clause 2.

source.place: Tag 0968, lemma-spectral-split, (2) implies (1), first paragraph; paragraph after Tag 096A, definition-w-local; quotient-map argument made explicit

proof.text: Conversely, suppose every connected component of $T$ has exactly one closed point. Step 4 provides a closed specialization of every $x$. Every such specialization lies in the component of $x$, so the component hypothesis makes it unique. Combined with clause 2, this proves equivalence of the two closed-point conditions, with closedness of $S$ retained on both sides. On affine spectra the definition of w-local in [sk-def-pe-wlocal] is therefore exactly the definition in [def-weil-pbc-w-local]. No assertion that uniqueness alone implies closedness is used.

source.place: Tag 0968, lemma-spectral-split, (2) implies (1); Tag 096A, definition-w-local, and following paragraph; Tag 0969 explains why closedness must be retained

proof.text: For clause 4, take $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. The localization $R_{\mathfrak m}$ is at $M=R\setminus\mathfrak m$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The image formula in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding] gives the image as the primes $\mathfrak p$ with $\mathfrak p\cap M=\varnothing$, equivalently $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$. In the Zariski topology, $\overline{\{\mathfrak p\}}=V(\mathfrak p)$: a closed set $V(I)$ contains $\mathfrak p$ exactly when $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$, and $V(\mathfrak p)$ is the smallest such set. Thus these are precisely the generalizations of $\mathfrak m$, which clause 2 already identifies with its connected component. This proves clause 4.

lean.statement: theorem spectralSpace_closedPoints_components (T : Type u) [TopologicalSpace T] [SpectralSpace T] (hclosed : IsClosed (closedPoints T)) : (CompactSpace (closedPoints T) ∧ T2Space (closedPoints T) ∧ TotallyDisconnectedSpace (closedPoints T)) ∧ ((∀ x : T, ∃! c : closedPoints T, x ⤳ c.val) → (∃ r : T → closedPoints T, Continuous r ∧ (∀ x : T, x ⤳ (r x).val) ∧ (∀ c : closedPoints T, r c.val = c) ∧ ∀ c : closedPoints T, r ⁻¹' {c} = connectedComponent c.val ∧ connectedComponent c.val = {x : T | x ⤳ c.val}) ∧ IsHomeomorph (ConnectedComponents.mk ∘ (Subtype.val : closedPoints T → T)) ∧ CompactSpace (ConnectedComponents T) ∧ T2Space (ConnectedComponents T) ∧ TotallyDisconnectedSpace (ConnectedComponents T)) ∧ ((∀ x : T, ∃! c : closedPoints T, c.val ∈ connectedComponent x) → ∀ x : T, ∃! c : closedPoints T, x ⤳ c.val) ∧ (WLocalSpace T ↔ ∀ x : T, ∃! c : closedPoints T, c.val ∈ connectedComponent x) ∧ (∀ (R : Type v) [CommRing R], IsWLocalRing R ↔ IsClosed (closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum R)) ∧ ∀ x : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃! c : closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum R), c.val ∈ connectedComponent x) ∧ (∀ (R : Type v) [CommRing R] [IsWLocalRing R] (m : Ideal R) [m.IsMaximal], connectedComponent (⟨m, inferInstance⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R) = Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime m))))
